title: Code Quality and Style
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of code quality and style and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply consistent naming in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Code Quality and Style is part of Debugging, Testing, and Software Quality. Start with consistent naming and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A reliable workflow turns assumptions into checks and uses errors, tests and logs as evidence instead of hiding failures.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A reliable workflow turns assumptions into checks and uses errors, tests and logs as evidence instead of hiding failures. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.text: For avoiding duplicate logic, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Write one positive test and one failure/edge test, then state what evidence would prove the check ran. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Code Quality and Style
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 203: Code Quality and Style
example_result <- 2 * 2
stopifnot(example_result == 4)
"check passed"
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: A successful assertion is useful evidence for one condition only; add negative and boundary tests too. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For code quality and style, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply code quality and style to a small synthetic example. Start with consistent naming, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the consistent naming idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.
content.expected_output: A reproducible code quality and style example or design sketch with the expected result, one checked edge or failure case, and a stated limitation.
hints: Start with “Consistent Naming” and identify the input and output before coding.
Prefer a small repeatable test and capture the result before changing the implementation.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
